_note: Day 6 shift: a minute of traffic to the website. Built by the generic path of LogGenerator (event "traffic"). The rules: the Requests a minute part is an "info" rule (a big number decides nothing: the sale is huge and real), the requests from each address are a "threshold" with an "exempt" browser (our own monitor), the pages and the browser are "allowed" rules (the browser has "odd_values": a polite crawler). The threat is the page /search?q= and the browser bot-kit/1.0 that repeat in bad logs.

comments.short: Joshua: No mistakes, but too few logs. Be quicker.

hud_line: Judge each visitor, not the crowd    On call: {on_call}

rules.name: Requests a minute
rules.text: A big number does not decide. It does not make traffic good or bad.
details: A sale can send 14,000 requests a minute, and all of them real.
rules.why: Look at what each visitor does. The size of the crowd decides nothing.

rules.name: From each address
rules.text: One visitor sends at most 40 requests a minute.
details: Our own monitor may send more: checking the site is its job.
rules.why: A person clicks a few times a minute. A bot sends hundreds.
rules.broken: sends far too many requests from one address

rules.name: Pages
rules.text: Real visitors look around: the shop, a product, the cart, the checkout.
details: A flood asks for one page, again and again.
rules.why: People wander through a site. A flood asks for the same page.

rules.name: Browser
rules.text: A real browser has a real name.
details: friendly-bot/2.1 is the search engine's crawler: allowed, but worth a look.
rules.why: Thousands of real visitors never share one made-up browser name.
rules.broken: comes from a browser name nobody real uses

decoys.reason: 14,000 requests is a huge crowd, but it is the sale: 12 from each address, many pages, a real browser.
The search engine's crawler is polite and allowed. It is under the limit, and it reads many pages.
600 requests from one address is a lot, but it is our own monitor checking the shop, and it is exempt.

story_logs.reason: {first}'s sale brought a huge crowd of real customers: 12 from each address and a real browser.

ok: {requests} requests tells you little by itself.
A crowd of {requests} can be real or not.
{each} from each address is a few clicks.
{each} a minute is a person's pace.
exempt: {each} is a lot, but this one is cleared to send it.
bad: {each} from one address is a bot's pace.

ok: Visitors who ask for {pages} are browsing.
bad: Only one page, again and again, is not shopping.

odd: {browser} is a known program, not a person.
bad: {browser} is not a browser anyone really uses.

1: New shift. A crowd and a flood look alike from far away. This time you judge each visitor.
Click a line to ask me about it. The clock is frozen while you learn.
Rules are in the RULEBOOK. Then LET PASS or REPORT.
2: Check all four lines on the card.
3: A huge crowd can be real. Look at what each visitor does.
4: The clock runs now. Good luck.

rulebook.intro: REPORT traffic that breaks a rule. LET PASS the rest, even a huge crowd.
rulebook.margin: Within %d of the limit is a bit odd, but still allowed.

messages.no_time: No time to ask. Decide now.
